stimuli.title: Urban Water Security
stimuli.text:
Water scarcity in cities is often described as a consequence of insufficient rainfall. Yet the availability of rainfall alone does not determine whether residents receive dependable water supplies. Urban water security depends equally on infrastructure, institutions, distribution practices and the condition of surrounding ecosystems.

Many cities draw water from distant rivers and reservoirs while losing a substantial portion through leaking pipes, unauthorised connections and inaccurate metering. Expanding supply without addressing these losses can increase financial and environmental costs. New pipelines and reservoirs may temporarily relieve shortages, but they do little to correct inefficient management. Consequently, cities may experience simultaneous infrastructure expansion and persistent water insecurity.

Demand is also distributed unequally. Well-served neighbourhoods may consume large quantities of treated water, whereas informal settlements often rely on expensive private suppliers or irregular communal sources. Such differences show that water security concerns not merely the total volume available but also affordability, reliability and equitable access.

Groundwater adds another complication. It provides an important buffer during interruptions in municipal supply, but excessive extraction can lower water tables and damage aquifers. Urban construction that covers permeable land with concrete further restricts natural recharge. Rainwater harvesting and the restoration of lakes, wetlands and drainage channels can therefore support long-term resilience, although their effectiveness depends on maintenance and local conditions.

A more sustainable strategy combines reliable measurement, leakage reduction, appropriate pricing, targeted support for vulnerable households, wastewater treatment and reuse, groundwater regulation and protection of local ecosystems. Pricing can encourage conservation, but poorly designed tariffs may burden poorer residents. Similarly, technological tools such as sensors and digital meters can improve monitoring, but they cannot substitute for accountable institutions.

Ultimately, urban water security is a governance challenge as much as an engineering challenge. Success should be judged not simply by the quantity of water supplied or the number of projects completed, but by whether residents receive safe, affordable and dependable water without compromising the resources needed by future generations.

explanations.pfrda:day3:a:q:22:r1: Section 36 provides an appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal ordinarily within 45 days. Section 38 provides a further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law ordinarily within 60 days, subject to statutory provisions for delay.

explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:02:r1: Section 36 provides an ordinary 45-day period, with statutory scope to condone delay on sufficient cause.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:03:r1: The stated FY 2030–31 objective is 50% of GDP with a ±1 percentage-point range.

explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:09:r1: A superior can delegate authority and responsibility for work, but cannot fully abdicate ultimate accountability.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:10:r1: Bond price and required yield move inversely because the fixed future cash flows are discounted at a higher rate when yield rises.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:11:r1: The importer will need dollars later, so buying (going long) US dollars forward locks in the future exchange rate.

explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:15:r1: Just-in-time systems minimise inventory buffers, so supplier or logistics disruption can halt production rapidly.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:16:r1: Section 123 permits dividend from eligible profits subject to statutory conditions, including the depreciation requirement.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:17:r1: Section 144 lists internal audit among services that the statutory auditor must not provide to the audited company, subject to the statutory framework.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:18:r1: An independent director can generally serve up to two consecutive terms, each up to five years, followed by the statutory cooling-off period.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:19:r1: The ordinary quorum is one-third of total strength or two directors, whichever is higher, subject to the Act's qualifications.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:21:r1: Personal remittances are current-account secondary income/transfers, not capital or portfolio investment flows.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:22:r1: A repo-rate cut generally eases monetary conditions and can reduce borrowing costs, though transmission is not mechanically one-for-one.
explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:23:r1: Ordinary Tier II is a voluntary savings account with flexible access, distinct from Tier I retirement-exit restrictions.

explanations.pfrda:day3:b:q:25:r1: The defining difference is when periodic annuity payments commence.

A strong response should show that technology expands access while trust, fraud prevention, grievance redressal, privacy, literacy and accountable institutions sustain adoption.
explanations.pfrda:day3:e:q:02:r1: Increasing water supply alone cannot solve urban water insecurity because leakages, inefficient distribution, weak institutions and environmental degradation also affect availability and reliability.
explanations.pfrda:day3:e:q:03:r1: Unequal access makes water security an equity issue because well-served neighbourhoods may receive abundant reliable water while poorer or informal settlements depend on costly or irregular sources.
explanations.pfrda:day3:e:q:04:r1: Excessive groundwater extraction can lower water tables and damage aquifers; urban construction that covers permeable land with concrete restricts natural recharge.
explanations.pfrda:day3:e:q:05:r1: Pricing can promote conservation but may burden poorer households if badly designed. Technology can improve monitoring but cannot substitute for accountable institutions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:e:q:06:r1: Urban water security requires integrated governance, efficient infrastructure, equitable distribution and ecological protection. Success should be judged by safe, affordable and dependable access without compromising future resources, not merely by supply volumes or projects completed.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:01:r1: For a large corpus at normal exit under the current rules, a non-government subscriber may ordinarily take up to 80% as lump sum (₹19.2 lakh of ₹24 lakh), while a government-sector subscriber may ordinarily take up to 60% (₹14.4 lakh), subject to applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:02:r1: Under the current All Citizen exit framework, completion of the prescribed 15-year subscription route can permit normal exit before age 60, subject to the applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:03:r1: For the applicable ₹8–12 lakh band, the current exit framework provides a special route allowing up to ₹6 lakh upfront and the balance through systematic unit redemption for at least six years, subject to the regulation.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:04:r1: At normal government-sector exit, the small-corpus rule permits full lump-sum withdrawal where the accumulated pension wealth is within the prescribed threshold; ₹7.8 lakh falls within that band.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:05:r1: Ordinary premature exit generally requires at least 80% of the corpus for annuity. 80% of ₹9 lakh = ₹7.2 lakh.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:06:r1: Death is governed by a separate exit treatment; the nominee/legal heir can receive the entire accumulated wealth, with other approved payout options also available under the applicable framework.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:07:r1: The current rule ordinarily requires a three-year interval between partial withdrawals, subject to the applicable conditions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:08:r1: Ordinary Tier II is a voluntary, relatively liquid account. It ordinarily permits withdrawal while Tier I remains active; it is distinct from Tier I exit/annuity restrictions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:09:r1: The Tier II Tax Saver variant is a special arrangement for eligible Central Government NPS subscribers and carries a three-year lock-in, unlike ordinary Tier II liquidity.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:10:r1: Under the 2026 NPS Vatsalya guidelines, up to two partial withdrawals are permitted before age 18 and up to two additional withdrawals between 18 and 21 after the prescribed fresh identity verification and subject to other conditions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:11:r1: For the applicable Vatsalya exit after majority, a corpus below ₹8 lakh may be withdrawn fully, subject to the prescribed conditions.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:12:r1: If no choice is exercised by age 21, the current Vatsalya guidelines prescribe transition to the specified higher-equity Multiple Scheme Framework variant of the same pension fund rather than an automatic cash payout.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:13:r1: On death of the minor subscriber, the accumulated wealth is payable to the appropriate guardian/nominee/legal heir, with the applicable option to transfer to an eligible NPS account.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:14:r1: The post-1 October 2022 restriction applies to opening a new APY account by a person who is or has been an income-tax payer; it does not automatically cancel a qualifying earlier account.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:15:r1: Under APY, the spouse receives the same guaranteed minimum pension after the subscriber's death; after both subscriber and spouse die, the nominee receives the prescribed pension wealth. The 60% family-payout rule belongs to UPS, not APY.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:16:r1: Full assured payout benchmark = 50% of ₹80,000 = ₹40,000 for 25 years (300 months). Proportionate payout = ₹40,000×180/300 = ₹24,000.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:17:r1: The lower corpus is ₹20 lakh; 60% is ₹12 lakh. A final withdrawal reduces the assured payout proportionately under the UPS framework.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:18:r1: For the stated qualifying voluntary-retirement case, the UPS assured periodic payout begins from the date of notional normal superannuation, while specified lump-sum/final-withdrawal benefits may be available at voluntary retirement.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:19:r1: The applicable NPS-Lite/Swavalamban small-corpus schedule permits full lump-sum withdrawal at normal exit where accumulated pension wealth does not exceed the specified ₹2 lakh threshold.
explanations.pfrda:day3:p:q:20:r1: Sukanya Samriddhi uses a balance-based education-withdrawal rule (up to 50% of the preceding financial year-end balance under the stated age/Class 10 condition). NPS Vatsalya uses a distinct contribution-based partial-withdrawal rule, currently up to 25% of contributions excluding returns for permitted purposes and subject to conditions.
